units.zh: 李嗣業，字嗣業，京兆高陵人。
units.en: Li Siye, whose courtesy name was also Siye, came from Gaoling in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Li Siye was his name, courtesy name Siye, a native of Gaoling in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 長七尺，膂力絕眾。
units.en: He stood seven feet tall, with strength of arm unmatched among his peers.
units.literal: He was seven chi in height, and his arm strength surpassed the multitude.

units.zh: 開元中，從安西都護來曜討十姓蘇祿，先登捕虜，累功署昭武校尉。
units.en: During the Kaiyuan period he served under Anxi Protector-General Lai Yao against Suluk of the Ten Surnames, scaling the heights first and taking captives; for repeated merit he was made a Defender of Zhaowu.
units.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he followed the Protector-General of Anxi, Lai Yao, to campaign against Suluk of the Ten Surnames; he was first to scale [the heights], captured prisoners, and for accumulated merit was appointed Defender of Zhaowu.

units.zh: 後應募安西，軍中初用陌刀，而嗣業尤善，每戰必為先鋒，所向摧北。
units.en: He later enlisted in the Anxi forces when the mo dao was first introduced to the troops; Siye excelled with it above all, invariably leading the van in battle and breaking the enemy wherever he charged.
units.literal: Later he enrolled in the Anxi army; the army had newly adopted the mo blade, and Siye was especially skilled; in every battle he was made vanguard, and wherever he went the enemy was crushed.

units.zh: 馬靈察為節度，出戰必與俱。
units.en: Under Military Commissioner Ma Lingcha, he always accompanied him on campaign.
units.literal: When Ma Lingcha became military commissioner, whenever he went out to fight Siye went with him.

units.zh: 高仙芝討勃律，署嗣業及中郎將田珍為左右陌刀將。
units.en: During Gao Xianzhi's expedition against Balur, Siye and Central Regiment Director Tian Zhen were appointed commanders of the left and right mo-blade units.
units.literal: When Gao Xianzhi campaigned against Balur, he appointed Siye and the Central Regiment Director Tian Zhen as left and right mo-blade commanders.

units.zh: 時吐蕃兵十萬屯娑勒城，據山瀕水，聯木作郛，以扼王師。
units.en: A Tibetan force of one hundred thousand held Suole Fort on the heights above the water, their linked timber walls blocking the imperial advance.
units.literal: At that time a hundred thousand Tibetan troops were encamped at Suole Fort, holding the mountains and bordering the water, linking timbers to make a palisade to block the royal army.

units.zh: 仙芝潛軍夜濟信圖河，令曰：「及午破賊，不者皆死。」
units.en: Xianzhi stole across the Xintu River at night with his army, declaring: "Break the enemy by noon, or every man dies."
units.literal: Xianzhi secretly led troops by night to cross the Xintu River, ordering: "By noon break the bandits, or all shall die."

units.zh: 嗣業提步士升山，頹石四面以擊賊，又樹大旗先走險，諸將從之。
units.en: Siye led infantry up the slope, hurling stones down on the enemy from all sides; planting his standard first over the difficult ground, the other commanders followed.
units.literal: Siye led foot soldiers up the mountain, rolling stones down on all sides to strike the bandits; he also planted a great banner and first took the dangerous route, and the generals followed him.

units.zh: 虜不虞軍至，因大潰，投崖谷死者十八。
units.en: The barbarians, caught unawares, broke and fled; as much as eight in ten of those who tumbled into gullies and ravines perished.
units.literal: The barbarians did not expect the army's arrival and so were greatly routed; eighteen-tenths of those who plunged off cliffs and into ravines died.

units.zh: 鼓而驅至勃律，禽其主，平之。
units.en: They beat the drums and pressed on to Balur, seized its ruler, and brought the region under control.
units.literal: Drumming the advance they drove to Balur, captured its lord, and pacified it.

units.zh: 授右威衛將軍。
units.en: He was made a general of the Right Majestic Guard.
units.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Majestic Guard.

units.zh: 從平石國及突騎施，以跳蕩先鋒加特進。
units.en: Serving in the subjugation of the Stone Kingdom and the Turgesh, he earned especial advancement as spearhead of the shock troops.
units.literal: He followed in the pacification of the Stone Kingdom and the Turgesh, and as vanguard in swift assault was granted especial advancement.

units.zh: 虜號為「神通大將」。
units.en: The enemy styled him the "Great General of Supernatural Might."
units.literal: The barbarians called him the "Great General of Divine Power."

units.zh: 初，仙芝特以計襲取石，其子出奔，因構諸胡共怨之，以告大食，連兵攻四鎮。
units.en: Xianzhi had earlier taken the Stone Kingdom by surprise; the ruler's son fled abroad and stirred the western peoples to common grievance, appealing to the Arabs to join forces against the Four Garrisons.
units.literal: Earlier, Xianzhi had relied on stratagem to seize the Stone Kingdom by surprise; the king's son fled into exile and therefore incited the various Hu peoples to common resentment, informing the Arabs, who allied troops to attack the Four Garrisons.

units.zh: 仙芝率兵二萬深入，為大食所敗，殘卒數千。
units.en: Xianzhi marched twenty thousand men deep into enemy country and was beaten by the Arab army, escaping with only a few thousand survivors.
units.literal: Xianzhi led twenty thousand troops deep in; they were defeated by the Arabs, with only several thousand survivors.

units.zh: 事急，嗣業謀曰：「將軍深履賊境，後援既絕，而大食乘勝，諸胡銳於鬥，我與將軍俱前死，尚誰報朝廷者？
units.en: With the crisis upon them, Siye urged: "General, you are deep in enemy land with no relief behind you, while the Arabs press their advantage and the western peoples are eager for battle. If we both die in the front ranks, who will carry word back to the court?
units.literal: The situation was urgent; Siye counseled, saying: "General, you have penetrated deep into bandit territory, rear support is already cut off, and the Arabs press their victory; the various Hu are keen to fight. If you and I both die in the van, who will still report to the court?

units.zh: 不如守白石嶺以為後計。」
units.en: Better to hold Baishi Ridge and plan from there."
units.literal: It would be better to hold Baishi Ridge as a plan for what comes after."

units.zh: 仙芝曰：「吾方收合餘盡，明日復戰。」
units.en: Xianzhi replied: "I am still rallying what is left of the army—we will fight again tomorrow."
units.literal: Xianzhi said: "I am just now gathering the remnants; tomorrow we fight again."

units.zh: 嗣業曰：「事去矣，不可坐須菹醢。」
units.en: Siye said: "The day is lost—we cannot sit here waiting to be butchered."
units.literal: Siye said: "The affair is already lost; we cannot sit and wait to be minced like meat."

units.zh: 即馳守白石，路既隘，步騎魚貫而前。
units.en: He rode at once to hold Baishi Pass; the road was so narrow that infantry and cavalry advanced in single file.
units.literal: He immediately galloped to hold Baishi; the road being narrow, foot and horse filed through in single file.

units.zh: 會拔汗那還兵，輜餉塞道不可騁，嗣業懼追及，手梃鏖擊，人馬斃僕者數十百，虜駭走，仙芝乃得還。
units.en: Ferghana troops were returning on the same road, their wagons choking the pass so that no one could ride freely. Fearing pursuit, Siye fought hand to hand with a club, killing scores of men and horses until the enemy fled in terror and Xianzhi could at last escape.
units.literal: It happened that Ferghana troops were returning; baggage and supplies blocked the road so that none could gallop free; Siye feared pursuit and with his own hand wielded a club in fierce combat; men and horses that fell numbered in the tens and hundreds; the barbarians fled in alarm, and only then could Xianzhi return.

units.zh: 表嗣業功，進右金吾大將軍，留為疏勒鎮使。
units.en: A memorial commended Siye's service; he was promoted to Grand General of the Right Golden Guard and left as commissioner of Shule Garrison.
units.literal: His memorial cited Siye's merit; he was advanced to Grand General of the Right Golden Guard and retained as commissioner of Shule Garrison.

units.zh: 城一隅阤，屢築輒壞，嗣業祝之，有白龍見，因其處蕝祠以祭，城遂不壞，漢耿恭故井久涸，禱已，泉復出。
units.en: One corner of the city wall kept collapsing whenever it was rebuilt. Siye prayed, a white dragon appeared, and he built a thatched shrine on the spot to offer sacrifice—the wall held thereafter. The ancient well of Geng Gong of Han had long run dry; after his prayers the spring flowed again.
units.literal: One corner of the wall collapsed; each time they built it again it fell; Siye prayed, and a white dragon appeared; at that spot they erected a thatched shrine to sacrifice, and the wall was no longer damaged; the old well of Han-era Geng Gong had long been dry, but after prayer the spring flowed again.

units.zh: 初討勃律也，通道蔥領，有大石塞隘，以足蹶之，抵穹壑，識者以為至誠所感雲。
units.en: On the earlier campaign against Balur, while opening the route through the Pamir passes, he kicked aside a boulder blocking the defile and sent it tumbling into the gorge—observers took this as heaven's answer to his utmost sincerity.
units.literal: When he first campaigned against Balur, they opened a route through the Congling Pass; a great stone blocked the narrow way; he kicked it with his foot and it rolled into the deep ravine; those who knew deemed it a response to his utmost sincerity.

units.zh: 天寶十二載，加驃騎大將軍。
units.en: In the twelfth year of Tianbao he was promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao he was given the additional title of Grand General of Agile Cavalry.

units.zh: 入朝，賜酒玄宗前，醉起舞，帝寵之，賜彩百、金皿五十物、錢十萬，曰：「為解酲具。」
units.en: On a visit to court he was given wine before the emperor; drunk, he rose to dance. Xuanzong delighted in him and granted a hundred lengths of silk, fifty gold vessels, and a hundred thousand cash, saying, "These are to help you sober up."
units.literal: He entered court; wine was bestowed before Xuanzong; drunk, he rose to dance; the emperor favored him and granted a hundred lengths of silk, fifty gold vessels, and a hundred thousand in cash, saying: "These are for sobering up."

units.zh: 安祿山反，肅宗追之，詔至，即引道，與諸將割臂盟曰：「所過郡縣，秋毫不可犯。」
units.en: When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong called him east; the moment the edict arrived he set out at the head of the column. He and the other generals cut their arms and swore: "In every district we pass, not the slightest harm may be done."
units.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Suzong summoned him; when the edict arrived, [Siye] immediately led the way, and with the generals cut their arms in covenant, saying: "In every commandery and county we pass, not a hair's breadth may be violated."

units.zh: 至鳳翔，上謁，帝喜曰：「今日卿至，賢於數萬眾。
units.en: At Fengxiang he was received in audience. The emperor said with joy, "Your arrival today is worth more to me than an army of tens of thousands.
units.literal: When he reached Fengxiang and presented himself, the emperor said with joy: "Today, with your arrival, you are worth more than tens of thousands of troops.

units.zh: 事之濟否，固在卿輩。」
units.en: Whether this enterprise succeeds rests with men like you."
units.literal: Whether the affair succeeds or not rests with you gentlemen."

units.zh: 乃詔與郭子儀、僕固懷恩掎角。
units.en: He was ordered to coordinate with Guo Ziyi and Pugu Huai'en in mutual support.
units.literal: He was then ordered to coordinate with Guo Ziyi and Pugu Huai'en in pincer action.

units.zh: 常為先鋒，以巨棓笞鬥，賊值，類崩潰。
units.en: He invariably led the van, wielding a great club in close combat; rebels who met him usually broke and fled.
units.literal: He was constantly made vanguard; with a great club he lashed in battle; when bandits encountered him they generally collapsed and fled.

units.zh: 進四鎮、伊西、北庭行軍兵馬使。
units.en: He was promoted to commander of the campaigning forces of the Four Garrisons, Yixi, and Beiting.
units.literal: He was advanced to Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons, Yixi, and Beiting campaigning forces.

units.zh: 廣平王收長安，嗣業統前軍，陣於香積祠北。
units.en: When the Prince of Guangping retook Chang'an, Siye led the vanguard and drew up north of the Xiangji Shrine.
units.literal: When the Prince of Guangping recovered Chang'an, Siye commanded the forward army and formed battle lines north of the Xiangji Shrine.

units.zh: 賊酋李歸仁擁精騎薄戰，王師注矢逐之，走未及營，賊大出，掩追騎，還蹂王師，於是亂不能陣。
units.en: The rebel commander Li Guiren led elite cavalry to press the attack. Imperial archers loosed a storm of arrows in pursuit, but before the pursuers reached the enemy camp the rebels poured out, enveloped them, and wheeled back to crush the imperial line—the army broke ranks and could not reform.
units.literal: The bandit chieftain Li Guiren led picked cavalry to press the fight; the royal army poured arrows in pursuit; before they could reach the camp the bandits came out in force, covered the pursuing horsemen, and turned back to trample the royal army; thus in disorder they could not form ranks.

units.zh: 嗣業謂子儀曰：「今日不蹈萬死取一生，則軍無類矣。」
units.en: Siye told Guo Ziyi, "Unless we risk everything today to win our one chance of survival, this army is finished."
units.literal: Siye said to Ziyi: "Today, if we do not tread through ten thousand deaths to seize one life, then the army will be wiped out to the last man."

units.zh: 即袒持長刀，大呼出陣前，殺數十人，陣復整。
units.en: He stripped to the waist, seized a long saber, and with a great shout charged to the front, killing dozens of men until the line steadied again.
units.literal: He immediately bared his torso, grasped a long blade, and with a great shout went out before the ranks, killing several tens of men, and the formation was restored.

units.zh: 步卒二千以陌刀、長柯斧堵進，所向無前。
units.en: Two thousand foot soldiers advanced with mo dao and long-shafted axes in a solid wall, irresistible wherever they struck.
units.literal: Two thousand foot soldiers with mo blades and long-shafted axes advanced in a blocking press, and wherever they went none could stand before them.

units.zh: 歸仁匿兵營左，覘軍勢，王分回紇銳兵擊其伏，嗣業出賊背合攻之，自日中至昃，斬首六萬級，填澗壑死幾半，賊東走，遂平長安。
units.en: Guiren had hidden troops to the left of his camp to watch the imperial line. The prince sent Uyghur elite cavalry against the ambush while Siye struck from the rear. From noon until dusk they took sixty thousand heads; nearly half the enemy died filling the ravines. The rebels fled east, and Chang'an was recovered.
units.literal: Guiren hid troops to the left of the camp and watched the army's strength; the prince detached Uyghur elite troops to strike the ambush; Siye came out behind the bandits and joined in the attack; from midday to late afternoon they beheaded sixty thousand; those who filled ravines and gullies in death were nearly half; the bandits fled east, and Chang'an was pacified.

units.zh: 進收東都，嗣業戰多。
units.en: In the advance to retake Luoyang, Siye fought in many battles.
units.literal: Advancing to recover the Eastern Capital, Siye fought in many engagements.

units.zh: 乃與張鎬、魯炅、來瑱、嗣吳王祗、李奐略定諸州。
units.en: He then joined Zhang Hao, Lu Jiong, Lai Tian, Prince Zhi of Wu, and Li Huan in bringing the surrounding prefectures under control.
units.literal: He then joined Zhang Hao, Lu Jiong, Lai Tian, Zhi the Successor Prince of Wu, and Li Huan in broadly pacifying the various prefectures.

units.zh: 兼衛尉卿，封虢國公，實封戶二百。
units.en: He was made concurrent Minister of the Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Guo with a fief of two hundred households.
units.literal: He was concurrently made Minister of the Guard; enfeoffed as Duke of Guo; with two hundred households of actual fief.

units.zh: 兼懷州刺史、北庭行營節度使。
units.en: He was also made Prefect of Huaizhou and Military Commissioner of the Beiting campaigning army.
units.literal: He was concurrently made Prefect of Huaizhou and Military Commissioner of the Beiting campaigning army.

units.zh: 與子儀等圍相州，師耄，諸將無功，獨嗣業被堅數奮，為諸軍冠。
units.en: Besieging Xiangzhou with Guo Ziyi and the others, the army was exhausted and the generals accomplished little; Siye alone, in full armor, charged again and again and stood first among all the forces.
units.literal: With Ziyi and others he besieged Xiangzhou; the army was worn out, the generals achieved nothing, but Siye alone, in heavy armor, charged repeatedly and was foremost among all the armies.

units.zh: 中流矢，臥帳中，方愈，忽聞金鼓聲，知與賊戰，大呼，創潰，血流數升卒。
units.en: Struck by a stray arrow, he lay in his tent convalescing when he suddenly heard gongs and drums and knew the army was in battle. He cried out; his wound reopened, blood poured forth in great streams, and he died.
units.literal: He was struck by a stray arrow and lay in his tent; just as he was recovering, he suddenly heard the sound of gongs and drums, knew the army was fighting the bandits, gave a great shout, his wound burst open, blood flowed in several sheng, and he died.

units.zh: 諡曰忠勇，贈武威郡王，給靈輿護還在所。
units.en: He was given the posthumous name Loyal and Valiant and posthumously made Prince of Wuwei; an imperial catafalque escorted his remains home.
units.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Valiant; he was given posthumously the title Prince of Wuwei Commandery; an imperial catafalque was granted to escort his remains back to his home.

units.zh: 葬日，使中人臨吊，中朝臣祖泣，塋給掃除十戶。
units.en: On the day of his burial palace envoys attended to mourn; court ministers wept as they saw him off; ten households were assigned to maintain his tomb.
units.literal: On the day of burial, palace envoys were sent to offer condolences; court ministers wept as they saw him off; ten households were granted to maintain his tomb.

units.zh: 嗣業忠毅憂國，不計居產，有宛馬十疋，前後賞賜，皆上於官以助軍雲。
units.en: Siye was loyal, resolute, and devoted to the state, caring nothing for his private wealth. He owned ten Ferghana horses and turned over every gift and reward to the government to support the army.
units.literal: Siye was loyal, resolute, and concerned for the state, heedless of his household property; he had ten Ferghana horses; rewards given him before and after he turned over to the government to aid the army.

units.zh: 子佐國，襲爵，曆丹王府長史。
units.en: His son Zuoguo inherited the title and served as chief clerk in the household of the Prince of Dan.
units.literal: His son Zuoguo inherited the title and served as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Dan's household.

units.zh: 卒，推嗣業功，贈宋州刺史。
units.en: When he died, in recognition of his father's service he was posthumously made Prefect of Songzhou.
units.literal: When he died, in recognition of Siye's merit he was posthumously made Prefect of Songzhou.

units.zh: 馬璘，岐州扶風人。
units.en: Ma Lin came from Fufeng in Qizhou.
units.literal: Ma Lin was his name, a native of Fufeng in Qizhou.

units.zh: 少孤，流蕩無業所。
units.en: Orphaned in youth, he wandered without a settled livelihood.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he drifted about with no settled occupation.

units.zh: 年二十，讀漢馬援傳，至「丈夫當死邊野，以馬革裹屍而歸」，慨然曰：「使吾祖勳業墜於地乎？」
units.en: At twenty he read the Han biography of Ma Yuan and came to the line, "A true man ought to die on the frontier wilds, his corpse wrapped in horsehide for the journey home." He exclaimed, "Shall my ancestor's achievements come to nothing?"
units.literal: At age twenty he read the Han biography of Ma Yuan; when he came to "A true man ought to die on the frontier wilds, his corpse wrapped in horsehide for the journey home," he said with emotion: "Shall my forebear's achievements fall to the ground?"

units.zh: 開元末，挾策從安西節度府，以奇勞，累遷金吾衛將軍。
units.en: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he went west to serve the Anxi military commission; for distinguished service he rose to general of the Golden Guard.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he took his plans and followed the Anxi military commission; for unusual merit he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Golden Guard.

units.zh: 至德初，王室多難，統精甲三千，自二庭赴鳳翔。
units.en: Early in the Zhide era, when the dynasty was in crisis, he led three thousand elite armored troops from the Two Courts to Fengxiang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhide the royal house faced many troubles; he led three thousand picked armored troops from the Two Courts to Fengxiang.

units.zh: 肅宗奇之，委以東討。
units.en: Suzong was impressed and entrusted him with the eastern campaign.
units.literal: Suzong marveled at him and entrusted him with the eastern campaign.

units.zh: 初戰衛南，以百騎破賊五千眾。
units.en: In his first battle at Weinan he routed five thousand rebels with a hundred horsemen.
units.literal: In his first battle at Weinan he broke five thousand bandits with a hundred horsemen.

units.zh: 從李光弼攻洛陽，史朝義眾十萬陣北邙山，旗鎧照日，諸疑，未敢擊。
units.en: Serving under Li Guangbi at Luoyang, he faced Shi Chaoyi's army of one hundred thousand drawn up on Mount Beimang, their banners and armor blazing in the sun. The commanders hesitated and dared not attack.
units.literal: Following Li Guangbi in the attack on Luoyang, Shi Chaoyi's force of a hundred thousand formed ranks on Mount Beimang; banners and armor blazed in the sun; the commanders hesitated and dared not strike.

units.zh: 璘率部士五百，薄賊屯，出入三反，眾披靡，乘之，賊遂潰。
units.en: Lin led five hundred of his men in a close assault on the rebel camp, charging in and out three times until the enemy line broke; pressing the advantage, he put the rebels to rout.
units.literal: Lin led five hundred men of his command, pressed close to the bandit encampment, went in and out three times; the masses were routed; pressing the advantage, the bandits then collapsed.

units.zh: 光弼曰：「吾用兵三十年，未見以少擊眾，雄捷如馬將軍者！」
units.en: Guangbi said, "In thirty years of command I have never seen anyone strike so boldly and swiftly against such odds as General Ma!"
units.literal: Guangbi said: "In thirty years of commanding troops I have never seen one who with few struck many, bold and swift as General Ma!"

units.zh: 遷試太常卿。
units.en: He was promoted to Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.
units.literal: He was transferred to Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 明年，吐蕃寇邊，詔璘移軍援河西。
units.en: The following year, when Tibetans raided the frontier, Lin was ordered to shift his army to aid Hexi.
units.literal: The next year Tibetans raided the border; an edict ordered Lin to shift his army to aid Hexi.

units.zh: 懷恩之叛，璘引還，間關轉鬥至鳳翔，虜圍已合，節度使孫志直嬰城守。
units.en: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, Lin turned back and fought his way through to Fengxiang, where the Tibetans had already closed the siege and Military Commissioner Sun Zhizhi was holding the city.
units.literal: When Huai'en rebelled, Lin led [his troops] back; through hardship he fought his way to Fengxiang; the barbarian siege was already complete; Military Commissioner Sun Zhizhi held the city in a closed defense.

units.zh: 璘令士持滿外向，突入縣門，不解甲出戰，背城陣。
units.en: Lin ordered his men to advance with bows fully drawn, burst through the county gate, and sally out without removing their armor, forming ranks with the city wall at their backs.
units.literal: Lin ordered his men to hold their bows fully drawn facing outward, burst through the county gate, went out to fight without doffing armor, and formed ranks with their backs to the wall.

units.zh: 虜潰，率輕騎追之，斬數千級，漂血丹渠。
units.en: The Tibetans broke; he led light cavalry in pursuit, taking several thousand heads until the Dan Canal ran red with blood.
units.literal: The barbarians collapsed; he led light cavalry in pursuit, beheading several thousand; blood floated on the Dan Canal.

units.zh: 帝引見尉勞，擢兼御史大夫。
units.en: The emperor received him, commended his service, and promoted him to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: The emperor summoned him, consoled and rewarded him, and promoted him to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 永泰初，拜四鎮行營節度、南道和蕃使。
units.en: Early in the Yongtai era he was made Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons campaigning army and envoy for Tibetan relations on the Southern Circuit.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons campaigning army and envoy for the Southern Circuit in relations with Tibet.

units.zh: 俄檢校工部尚書，北庭行營、邠甯節度使。
units.en: Soon after he was made Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of the Beiting campaigning army and Binning circuit.
units.literal: Shortly he was made Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of the Beiting campaigning army and Binning.

units.zh: 元日，有卒犯盜，或曰宜赦，璘曰：「赦之，則人將伺其日為盜。」
units.en: On New Year's Day a soldier was caught stealing. Some urged a pardon, but Lin said, "If we pardon him today, men will mark the calendar for their thefts."
units.literal: On New Year's Day a soldier committed theft; some said he ought to be pardoned; Lin said: "If we pardon him, then people will watch for that day to steal."

units.zh: 遂戮之。
units.en: He had the man executed.
units.literal: He then had him executed.

units.zh: 天大旱，裏巷為土龍聚巫以禱，璘曰：「旱由政不修。」
units.en: During a severe drought the townspeople erected earth dragons and gathered shamans to pray for rain. Lin said, "Drought comes from failure to govern well."
units.literal: A great drought came; in the lanes people made earth dragons and gathered shamans to pray; Lin said: "Drought comes from failure to govern well."

units.zh: 即命撤之。
units.en: He ordered them taken down at once.
units.literal: He immediately ordered them removed.

units.zh: 明日雨，是歲大穰。
units.en: Rain fell the next day, and that year brought a great harvest.
units.literal: The next day it rained, and that year the harvest was abundant.

units.zh: 未幾，徙涇原，權知鳳翔、隴右節度副使，四鎮、北庭如舊，復以鄭、潁二州隸之。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to Jingyuan as acting deputy military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou, retaining the Four Garrisons and Beiting as before, with Zheng and Ying prefectures added to his command.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to Jingyuan, with acting authority as deputy military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou; the Four Garrisons and Beiting as before, and again Zheng and Ying prefectures were placed under his command.

units.zh: 大曆八年，吐蕃內寇，渾瑊戰宜祿，不利。
units.en: In the eighth year of Dali the Tibetans raided inland; Hun Jian fought them at Yilu and was defeated.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Dali Tibetans raided inward; Hun Jian fought at Yilu with an unfavorable outcome.

units.zh: 璘設伏潘原，與瑊合擊破之，俘級數萬。
units.en: Lin laid an ambush at Panyuan and, joining Hun Jian, routed the Tibetans, taking tens of thousands of captives and heads.
units.literal: Lin set an ambush at Panyuan and with Jian joined in a combined attack that broke them; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: 進檢校尚書右僕射。
units.en: He was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: He was advanced to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 明年，入朝，求宰相，以檢校左僕射知省事，進撫風郡王。
units.en: The following year he came to court seeking the chancellorship and was made Acting Left Vice Director managing court affairs, advanced to Prince of Fufeng.
units.literal: The next year he entered court, sought the chancellorship, was made Acting Left Vice Director managing court affairs, and advanced to Prince of Fufeng Commandery.

units.zh: 十一年，卒於軍，年五十六。
units.en: In the eleventh year he died in camp at the age of fifty-six.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he died in camp, aged fifty-six.

units.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰武。
units.en: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses with the posthumous name Martial.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses; his posthumous title was Martial.

units.zh: 璘少學術，而武幹絕倫。
units.en: Lin had little scholarly learning, yet his martial gifts were without peer.
units.literal: Lin had little scholarship, yet his martial talent was without peer.

units.zh: 遭時屯棘，以忠力奮。
units.en: In a time of crisis he rose through loyalty and martial prowess.
units.literal: Meeting a time of hardship and thorns, he rose through loyalty and force.

units.zh: 在涇八年，繕屯壁，為戰守具，令肅不殘，人樂為用，虜不敢犯，為中興銳將。
units.en: For eight years at Jingyuan he repaired walls and stockades, equipped his forces for attack and defense, kept discipline without cruelty, and won willing service from his men—the barbarians dared not intrude. He was among the finest generals of the restoration.
units.literal: Eight years at Jing, he repaired walls and stockades, prepared equipment for attack and defense, kept orders strict without cruelty, men gladly served him, barbarians dared not intrude; he was a sharp general of the restoration.

units.zh: 初，涇軍乏財，帝諷李抱玉讓鄭、潁，璘因得裒積，且前後賜賚無算，家富不貲。
units.en: The Jing army had once been short of funds; the emperor had hinted that Li Baoyu yield Zheng and Ying, and Lin thereby amassed stores. Countless gifts followed, until his household wealth was beyond reckoning.
units.literal: Earlier the Jing army lacked funds; the emperor hinted that Li Baoyu should yield Zheng and Ying; Lin thereby amassed stores, and moreover rewards before and after were beyond counting; his household wealth was beyond measure.

units.zh: 治第京師，侈甚，其寢堂無慮費錢二十萬緡。
units.en: He built a mansion in the capital of staggering extravagance; the sleeping hall alone cost no less than two hundred thousand strings of cash.
units.literal: He built a mansion in the capital, extravagantly; its sleeping hall alone cost no less than two hundred thousand strings of cash.

units.zh: 方璘在軍，守者覆以油幔。
units.en: While Lin remained in the field, his stewards kept it covered with oiled awnings.
units.literal: While Lin was still in the army, the guardians covered it with oiled awnings.

units.zh: 及喪歸，都人爭入觀，假稱故吏入赴吊者日數百。
units.en: When his body was brought home, the people of the capital crowded in to see it; hundreds each day posed as former subordinates come to mourn.
units.literal: When his funeral returned, the capital people vied to enter and view it; those who falsely claimed to be old subordinates coming to mourn numbered hundreds each day.

units.zh: 德宗在東宮聞之，不喜。
units.en: The crown prince, later Dezong, heard of this and took offense.
units.literal: Dezong, then in the Eastern Palace, heard of it and was displeased.

units.zh: 及即位，乃禁第捨不得逾制，詔毀璘中寢及宦人劉忠翼第。
units.en: On his accession he forbade mansions that exceeded regulations and ordered Lin's central hall and the estate of the eunuch Liu Zhongyi torn down.
units.literal: When he took the throne, he forbade mansions from exceeding regulations and ordered the destruction of Lin's central sleeping hall and the mansion of the eunuch Liu Zhongyi.

units.zh: 璘家懼，悉籍亭館入之官。
units.en: Lin's family, in fear, registered all their pavilions and lodges with the government.
units.literal: Lin's family in fear registered all pavilions and lodges with the government.

units.zh: 其後賜群臣宴，多在璘山池。
units.en: Thereafter imperial banquets for the ministers were often held at Lin's hill and ponds.
units.literal: Thereafter when the emperor granted banquets to ministers, they were often held at Lin's hill and ponds.

units.zh: 而子弟無行，財亦尋盡。
units.en: But his sons and younger brothers were dissolute, and the fortune was soon spent.
units.literal: Yet his sons and younger brothers were without conduct, and the wealth was soon exhausted.

units.zh: 李抱玉，本安興貴曾孫，世居河西，善養馬。
units.en: Li Baoyu was a great-grandson of An Xinggui; his clan had long lived in Hexi and was skilled at raising horses.
units.literal: Li Baoyu was originally a great-grandson of An Xinggui; his clan had long dwelt in Hexi and was skilled at raising horses.

units.zh: 始名重璋，閑騎射，少從軍。
units.en: Born Chongzhang, he was skilled in mounted archery and entered the army in youth.
units.literal: His original name was Chongzhang; he was skilled in mounted archery and entered the army young.

units.zh: 其為人沈毅有謀，尤忠謹，李光弼引為裨校。
units.en: Deep, resolute, and shrewd, he was above all loyal and careful; Li Guangbi took him on as a staff officer.
units.literal: As a man he was deep, resolute, and resourceful, especially loyal and careful; Li Guangbi took him as a staff officer.

units.zh: 天寶末，玄宗以其戰河西有功，為改今名。
units.en: Late in the Tianbao era Xuanzong renamed him for his merit fighting in Hexi.
units.literal: At the end of Tianbao Xuanzong, because of his merit fighting in Hexi, changed his name to the present one.

units.zh: 祿山亂，守南陽，斬賊使。
units.en: When the rebellion broke out he held Nanyang and beheaded the rebel envoy.
units.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he held Nanyang and beheaded the rebel envoy.

units.zh: 至德二載，上言：「世占涼州，恥與逆臣共宗。」
units.en: In the second year of Zhide he petitioned: "Our clan has long held Liangzhou; we are shamed to share a surname with the traitor."
units.literal: In the second year of Zhide he submitted a memorial: "Our clan has long held Liangzhou; we are shamed to share a surname with the traitor."

units.zh: 有詔賜之姓，因徙籍京兆，舉族以李為氏。
units.en: An edict granted him the imperial surname Li; his household register was moved to Jingzhao, and the whole clan took Li as their name.
units.literal: An edict granted him the imperial surname; his registry was moved to Jingzhao, and the whole clan took Li as their surname.

units.zh: 進至右羽林大將軍，知軍事，擢陳鄭潁亳節度使。
units.en: He rose to Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest with charge of military affairs and was made Military Commissioner of Chen, Zheng, Ying, and Bo.
units.literal: He was advanced to Grand General of the Right Feathered Forest, managed military affairs, and was promoted to Military Commissioner of Chen, Zheng, Ying, and Bo.

units.zh: 史思明已破東都，兇焰勃然，鼓而行，自謂無前。
units.en: Shi Siming had already seized Luoyang; his power blazed, and drumming his advance he deemed himself invincible.
units.literal: Shi Siming had already taken the Eastern Capital; his fierce flame blazed; drumming as he marched, he deemed himself without rival.

units.zh: 光弼壁河陽拒之，使抱玉守南城。
units.en: Guangbi entrenched at Heyang to block him and left Baoyu to hold the southern city.
units.literal: Guangbi fortified at Heyang to resist him and ordered Baoyu to hold the southern city.

units.zh: 賊急攻，抱玉縱奇兵出，表裏俘殺甚眾。
units.en: When the rebels pressed the attack, Baoyu sent surprise forces out from within and without, capturing and killing a great many.
units.literal: The bandits pressed the attack fiercely; Baoyu unleashed surprise troops outward; inside and outside they captured and killed in great numbers.

units.zh: 賊乃舍去，從光弼戰，大敗，因不能西。
units.en: The rebels then withdrew; following Guangbi into battle they were routed and could advance no farther west.
units.literal: The bandits then abandoned [the siege] and followed Guangbi in battle; they were greatly defeated and thus could not advance west.

units.zh: 差功第一，封欒城縣公。
units.en: His merit was ranked first, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Luancheng County.
units.literal: His merit was ranked first; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Luancheng County.

units.zh: 代宗立，兼澤潞節度使，統相、衛、儀、邢十一州兵。
units.en: When Daizong succeeded, Baoyu was also made Military Commissioner of Ze and Lu, commanding troops from eleven prefectures including Xiang, Wei, Yi, and Xing.
units.literal: When Daizong took the throne, [Baoyu] was concurrently made Military Commissioner of Ze and Lu and commanded the troops of eleven prefectures including Xiang, Wei, Yi, and Xing.

units.zh: 以功授司空，兼兵部尚書，武威郡王。
units.en: For his service he was made Minister of Works and concurrent Minister of War, with the title Prince of Wuwei.
units.literal: For merit he was made Minister of Works, concurrently Minister of War, and Prince of Wuwei Commandery.

units.zh: 懇辭王爵，徙涼國公，進司徒。
units.en: He earnestly declined the princely title and was made Duke of Liang, then promoted to Minister over the Masses.
units.literal: He earnestly declined the princely title and was transferred to Duke of Liang, then advanced to Minister over the Masses.

units.zh: 廣德中，吐蕃入寇，帝次陝，群盜遍南山五穀間，東距虢，西抵岐，椎剽不勝計。
units.en: During the Guangde era the Tibetans raided inland while the emperor halted at Shan. Bandits spread through the five valleys of the Southern Mountains from Guo in the east to Qi in the west, plundering beyond reckoning.
units.literal: In the Guangde era Tibetans raided inward; the emperor halted at Shan; bandits spread throughout the five valleys of the Southern Mountains, east to Guo and west to Qi, plundering beyond count.

units.zh: 詔太子賓客薛景仙為南山五溪穀防禦使，引兵招捕，久不克。
units.en: The Prince's Guest Xue Jingxian was made Defender of the Five Streams and Valleys of the Southern Mountains and led troops to hunt the bandits down, but for a long time could not subdue them.
units.literal: An edict made the Prince's Guest Xue Jingxian Defender of the Five Streams and Valleys of the Southern Mountains; he led troops to recruit and capture them, but for long could not overcome them.

units.zh: 更詔抱玉討賊。
units.en: The court then ordered Baoyu to suppress the bandits.
units.literal: The edict was changed to order Baoyu to campaign against the bandits.

units.zh: 抱玉盡得賊株柢蹊隧，分兵守諸穀，使牙將李崇客精騎四百，自桃林、虢川襲之。
units.en: Baoyu traced the bandits' lairs and routes to the last, garrisoned the valleys, and sent his adjutant Li Chongke with four hundred elite horsemen to strike from Taolin and Guochuan.
units.literal: Baoyu fully learned the bandits' roots, lairs, and paths; he divided troops to guard the various valleys and sent his adjutant Li Chongke with four hundred picked horsemen to strike them from Taolin and Guochuan.

units.zh: 賊帥高玉脫身走城固，山南西道張獻誠禽以獻，悉索支黨斬之。
units.en: The bandit leader Gao Yu fled to Chenggu; Zhang Xiancheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured him and sent him in; all his followers were hunted down and executed.
units.literal: The bandit chief Gao Yu escaped to Chenggu; Zhang Xiancheng of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan captured and presented him; all associates were sought out and beheaded.

units.zh: 不閱旬，五穀平。
units.en: Within ten days the five valleys were pacified.
units.literal: Within less than ten days the five valleys were pacified.

units.zh: 即詔抱玉權鳳翔、隴右節度，抱玉懇讓司徒，故以尚書左僕射同中書門下平章事，河西、隴右副元帥。
units.en: Baoyu was then given acting command of Fengxiang and Longyou. He declined the Grand Tutorship and was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Deputy Commander of Hexi and Longyou.
units.literal: He was immediately ordered to act as Military Commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou; Baoyu earnestly declined the Grand Tutorship, and so was made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Deputy Commander of Hexi and Longyou.

units.zh: 又讓僕射，故還為兵部尚書。
units.en: He declined the vice directorship as well and was returned to his post as Minister of War.
units.literal: He again declined the Vice Directorship and therefore returned to Minister of War.

units.zh: 大曆二年，來朝。
units.en: In the second year of Dali he came to court.
units.literal: In the second year of Dali he came to court.

units.zh: 久之，加山南西道副元帥兼節度使，屯鷫厔。
units.en: Before long he was also made Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, with headquarters at Zhouzhi.
units.literal: After long he was given the additional titles of Deputy Commander and Military Commissioner of the Southwestern Circuit of Shannan, and encamped at Zhouzhi.

units.zh: 抱玉兼三節度、三副元帥，位望隆赫。
units.en: Baoyu held three military commissions and three deputy commands; his rank and prestige were immense.
units.literal: Baoyu concurrently held three military commissions and three deputy commands; his position and prestige were lofty and brilliant.

units.zh: 乃上言：「隴坻達扶、文，綿地二千里，虜孔道不一，梁、岷重則關輔輕。
units.en: He memorialized: "From Longqi to Fu and Wen the territory spans two thousand li, with many barbarian passes. If Liang and Min are overburdened, Guan and Fu are left exposed.
units.literal: He then submitted a memorial: "From Longqi to Fu and Wen stretches two thousand li; the barbarians' passes are not one; if Liang and Min are weighted heavily, then Guan and Fu are made light.

units.zh: 願擇能臣，帥西道當一面，臣得專事關、隴。」
units.en: Let a capable minister hold the western front alone, that I may devote myself wholly to Guan and Long."
units.literal: I wish to select a capable minister to command the western circuit on one front, so that I may devote myself solely to Guan and Long."

units.zh: 帝多其讓，許之。
units.en: The emperor approved his modesty and granted the request.
units.literal: The emperor praised his yielding and granted it.

units.zh: 抱玉在鎮十餘年，雖無破虜功，而禁暴安人，為將臣之良。
units.en: Baoyu held his command for more than ten years. Though he won no great victories over foreign foes, he suppressed violence and kept the people at peace—a model among commanders.
units.literal: Baoyu was in his command more than ten years; though without merit in breaking barbarians, he forbade violence and settled the people, and was a good among generals and ministers.

units.zh: 卒，年七十四，贈太保，諡曰昭武。
units.en: He died at seventy-four, posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Illustrious Martial.
units.literal: He died, aged seventy-four; posthumously made Grand Guardian; posthumous title Illustrious Martial.

units.zh: 從父弟 抱真從父弟抱真。
units.en: Younger cousin: Baozhen.
units.literal: Younger cousin by the father's line: Baozhen. Younger cousin by the father's line: Baozhen.

units.zh: 抱真字太玄，沈慮而斷。
units.en: Baozhen, courtesy name Taixuan, was deep-thinking and decisive.
units.literal: Baozhen's courtesy name was Taixuan; he was deep in thought and decisive.

units.zh: 抱玉屬以軍事，授汾州別駕。
units.en: Baoyu entrusted him with military affairs and made him Vice-Prefect of Fenzhou.
units.literal: Baoyu entrusted him with military affairs and appointed him Vice-Prefect of Fenzhou.

units.zh: 僕固懷恩反，陷焉，挺身歸京師。
units.en: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, Baozhen was caught in the revolt but made his way back to the capital.
units.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, [Baozhen] was trapped there; he threw himself forward and returned to the capital.

units.zh: 代宗以懷恩倚回紇，所將朔方兵精，憂之，召抱真問狀，答曰：「郭子儀嘗領朔方軍，人多德之。
units.en: Daizong, worried that Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and commanded elite Shuofang troops, summoned Baozhen for counsel. He replied, "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang army, and the men still honor him.
units.literal: Daizong, because Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and the Shuofang troops he led were elite, was worried; he summoned Baozhen to inquire the situation; he answered: "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang army; many owe him gratitude.

units.zh: 懷恩欺其下曰，'子儀為朝恩所殺。
units.en: Huai'en has deceived his men, telling them that Ziyi was killed by Chao'en.
units.literal: Huai'en deceived his subordinates, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by Chao'en.

units.zh: '今起而用，是伐其謀，兵可不戰解也。」
units.en: If we restore him to command, Huai'en's scheme collapses and the army will disperse without a fight."
units.literal: Now if we raise and employ [Ziyi], this cuts against his plot, and the army can be dissolved without battle."

units.zh: 既而懷恩敗，如抱真策。
units.en: Huai'en was soon defeated, just as Baozhen had predicted.
units.literal: Shortly after, Huai'en was defeated, just as Baozhen had strategized.

units.zh: 遷殿中少監、陳鄭澤潞節度留後。
units.en: He was made Vice-Director of the Palace Domestic Service and acting military commissioner of Chen, Zheng, Ze, and Lu.
units.literal: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Palace Domestic Service and Acting Military Commissioner of Chen, Zheng, Ze, and Lu.

units.zh: 既謝，因言：「百姓勞逸在牧守，願得一州以自試。」
units.en: On taking leave he said, "The people's welfare depends on their local governors. Grant me one prefecture to prove myself."
units.literal: After he thanked [for the appointment], he said: "The people's toil and rest depend on the prefects and governors; I wish to receive one prefecture to test myself."

units.zh: 更授澤州刺史，兼澤潞節度副使。
units.en: He was made Prefect of Zezhou and deputy military commissioner of Ze and Lu.
units.literal: He was then given Prefect of Zezhou, concurrently Deputy Military Commissioner of Ze and Lu.

units.zh: 徙懷州，仍為懷澤潞觀察留後，凡八年。
units.en: He was transferred to Huaizhou, remaining acting observation commissioner of Huai, Ze, and Lu for eight years in all.
units.literal: He was moved to Huaizhou, still Acting Observation Commissioner of Huai, Ze, and Lu, for eight years in all.

units.zh: 抱真策山東有變，澤、潞兵所走集，乘戰伐後，賦重人困，軍伍雕刓，乃籍戶三丁擇一，蠲其徭租，給弓矢，令閑月得曹偶習射，歲終大校，親按籍第能否賞責。
units.en: Baozhen foresaw unrest in the east. Ze and Lu were where armies gathered, and repeated campaigns had left taxes crushing and the ranks depleted. He registered households and drafted one man in three, exempting them from corvée and rent, arming them with bows and organizing off-season archery practice. Each year he personally inspected them and rewarded or punished according to merit.
units.literal: Baozhen judged that trouble would arise in the east; Ze and Lu were where troops converged; after campaigns taxes were heavy and the people distressed, the army ranks depleted; he therefore registered households and chose one from every three men, exempted their corvée and rent, supplied bows and arrows, ordered that in idle months they might gather in groups to practice archery; at year's end a great review was held, and he personally checked the registers to rank ability and reward or punish.

units.zh: 比三年，皆為精兵，舉所部得成卒二萬，既不稟於官，而府庫實。
units.en: Within three years he had forged an elite force of twenty thousand trained men, supplied from his own treasury rather than the state coffers.
units.literal: Within three years all were elite troops; throughout his command he had twenty thousand trained soldiers; they were not supplied from the government, yet the treasury was full.

units.zh: 乃曰：「軍可用矣。」
units.en: He declared, "The army is ready."
units.literal: He then said: "The army is fit for use."

units.zh: 繕甲淬兵，遂雄山東，天下稱昭義步兵為諸軍冠。
units.en: He repaired armor and honed weapons until his domain dominated the east, and the Zhaoyi infantry were hailed as the finest in the empire.
units.literal: He repaired armor and tempered weapons; he then dominated the east; all under heaven called the Zhaoyi infantry foremost among the armies.

units.zh: 久之，為澤潞節度行軍司馬。
units.en: Before long he was made campaigning marshal of the Ze and Lu commission.
units.literal: After long he was made campaigning marshal of the Ze and Lu military commission.

units.zh: 會昭義節度李承昭病，詔抱真權磁邢兵馬留後。
units.en: When Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Li Chengzhao fell ill, Baozhen was ordered to act as commander of the Ci and Xing forces.
units.literal: It happened that Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Li Chengzhao fell ill; an edict ordered Baozhen to act as Acting Commander of Ci and Xing troops.

units.zh: 德宗嗣位，檢校工部尚書，領昭義節度使。
units.en: When Dezong succeeded, Baozhen was made Acting Minister of Works and full Zhaoyi Military Commissioner.
units.literal: When Dezong succeeded, [Baozhen] was made Acting Minister of Works and took charge as Zhaoyi Military Commissioner.

units.zh: 建中中，田悅反，圍邢及臨洺，詔抱真與河東馬燧合神策兵救之，敗悅於雙岡，斬其將楊朝光，又破之臨洺，遂解臨洺、邢之圍。
units.en: During the Jianzhong era Tian Yue rebelled and besieged Xing and Linming. Baozhen joined Ma Sui of Hedong and the Shence army in relief, defeated Yue at Shuanggang, beheaded his general Yang Chaoguang, routed him again at Linming, and lifted both sieges.
units.literal: In the Jianzhong era Tian Yue rebelled and besieged Xing and Linming; an edict ordered Baozhen and Hedong's Ma Sui to join Shence troops in relief; they defeated Yue at Shuanggang, beheaded his general Yang Chaoguang, broke him again at Linming, and thus lifted the sieges of Linming and Xing.

units.zh: 以功檢校兵部尚書。
units.en: For this service he was made Acting Minister of War.
units.literal: For merit he was made Acting Minister of War.

units.zh: 復與悅戰洹水，走之。
units.en: He fought Yue again on the Huan River and drove him off.
units.literal: Again he fought Yue at the Huan River and put him to flight.

units.zh: 進圍魏，悅戰城下，大敗。
units.en: Pressing the siege of Wei, he defeated Yue in battle below the walls.
units.literal: Advancing to besiege Wei, Yue fought below the walls and was greatly defeated.

units.zh: 進檢校尚書右僕射。
units.en: He was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: He was advanced to Acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 會硃滔、王武俊反，救悅，抱真退保魏。
units.en: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled to rescue Yue, Baozhen fell back to defend Wei.
units.literal: It happened that Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled to rescue Yue; Baozhen withdrew to hold Wei.

units.zh: 帝蒼卒狩奉天，聞問，諸將皆哭，各引麾下還屯。
units.en: When the emperor fled in haste to Fengtian, the generals wept at the news and each led his troops back to camp.
units.literal: The emperor in haste went to hunt at Fengtian; when the news came, all the generals wept and each led his followers back to encamp.

units.zh: 于時，李希烈陷汴，李納反鄆，李懷光相次反河中，抱真獨以數州截然橫絕潰叛中，離沮其奸，為群盜所憚。
units.en: Li Xilie had seized Bian, Li Na rebelled at Yan, and Li Huai'guang rose in Hezhong in turn. Baozhen alone held several prefectures as a bulwark amid the collapse, thwarting rebel designs and inspiring fear among the rebel hosts.
units.literal: At that time Li Xilie took Bian, Li Na rebelled at Yan, Li Huai'guang in succession rebelled in Hezhong; Baozhen alone with several prefectures stood sharply athwart the collapsing rebellion, disrupting their plots, and was feared by the band of rebels.

units.zh: 興元初，檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事，繇倪國公進義陽郡王。
units.en: Early in the Xingyuan era he was made Acting Left Vice Director and Concurrent Grand Councilor, advanced from Duke of Niguo to Prince of Yiyang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was made Acting Left Vice Director and Concurrent Grand Councilor; from Duke of Niguo he advanced to Prince of Yiyang Commandery.

units.zh: 硃滔悉幽薊兵與回紇圍貝州，以應硃泚。
units.en: Zhu Tao mustered the armies of You and Ji with Uyghur allies to besiege Beizhou in support of Zhu Ci.
units.literal: Zhu Tao mustered the troops of You and Ji with the Uyghurs to besiege Beizhou in response to Zhu Ci.

units.zh: 而希烈既竊名號，則欲臣制諸叛，眾稍離。
units.en: Once Xilie had claimed the throne himself, he sought to dominate the other rebels, and their alliance began to fray.
units.literal: But once Xilie had usurped the imperial title, he wished to make the other rebels his subjects; the masses gradually separated.

units.zh: 天子下罪己詔，並赦群盜。
units.en: The emperor issued an edict of self-reproach and granted a general amnesty to the rebels.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven issued a self-reproach edict and pardoned all the rebels together.

units.zh: 抱真乃遣客賈林以大義說武俊，使合從擊滔，武俊許諾，而內猶豫。
units.en: Baozhen sent his retainer Jia Lin to persuade Wang Wujun on grounds of loyalty to join against Zhu Tao. Wujun agreed outwardly but remained undecided within.
units.literal: Baozhen then sent his guest Jia Lin to persuade Wujun with great principle to join in alliance against Tao; Wujun promised, yet inwardly hesitated.

units.zh: 抱真將自造其壁，諉軍事于司馬盧玄卿曰：「吾此行，系時安危，使遂不還，部勒以聽天子命，惟子；
units.en: Baozhen resolved to visit Wujun in person. He entrusted military affairs to his marshal Lu Xuanqing, saying, "This journey bears on the fate of the realm. If I do not return, hold the army to the emperor's command—that is yours alone;
units.literal: Baozhen was about to go in person to his camp; he entrusted military affairs to his marshal Lu Xuanqing, saying: "This journey of mine bears on the safety of the times; if I do not return, command the troops to obey the Son of Heaven's orders—this is yours alone;

units.zh: 勵兵東向，雪吾之恥，亦唯子。」
units.en: to lead the army east and avenge my disgrace—that too is yours alone."
units.literal: to urge the army eastward and wipe away my shame—this too is yours alone."

units.zh: 即以數騎馳入見武俊，曰：「泚、希烈爭竊帝號，滔攻貝州，此其志皆欲自肆於天下。
units.en: He rode in with only a few horsemen to see Wujun. "Ci and Xilie vie for the throne, and Tao attacks Beizhou—they all mean to rule the empire for themselves.
units.literal: He immediately took several horsemen and galloped in to see Wujun, saying: "Ci and Xilie vie to usurp the imperial title; Tao attacks Beizhou—their aim is all to indulge themselves over the empire.

units.zh: 足下既不能與競長雄，舍九葉天子而臣反虜乎？
units.en: If you cannot match them, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations to serve rebels?
units.literal: If you, sir, cannot compete with them for supremacy, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and serve the rebel barbarians?

units.zh: 且詔書罪己，禹、湯之心也。
units.en: The emperor's edict of self-reproach is the spirit of Yu and Tang.
units.literal: Moreover the edict reproaches himself—this is the heart of Yu and Tang.

units.zh: 方上暴露播越，公能自安乎？」
units.en: The sovereign wanders in hardship and exile—can you rest at ease?"
units.literal: Just now the sovereign is exposed in the open, cast about in exile—can you, sir, be at ease?"

units.zh: 因持武俊，涕下交頤，武俊亦感泣，左右皆泣。
units.en: He seized Wang Wujun's hands, tears streaming down his face. Wujun wept as well, and all present wept with them.
units.literal: He then seized Wujun; tears streamed down both cheeks; Wujun too was moved to weeping, and those at his side all wept.

units.zh: 退臥帳中，甘寢久之。
units.en: Wujun withdrew to his tent and slept soundly for a long while.
units.literal: He withdrew and lay in his tent, sleeping sweetly for a long while.

units.zh: 武俊感其不疑，乃益恭，指心誓天曰：「此身已許公死矣！」
units.en: Moved by Baozhen's trust, Wujun grew all the more respectful. Pointing to his heart he swore to heaven, "This life is yours to the death!"
units.literal: Wujun, moved that [Baozhen] did not doubt him, became all the more respectful; pointing to his heart he swore to Heaven: "This body is already pledged to die for you, sir!"

units.zh: 食訖，約為昆弟而別。
units.en: After the meal they pledged brotherhood and parted.
units.literal: When the meal was finished, they pledged brotherhood and parted.

units.zh: 旦日合戰，大破滔經城。
units.en: The next day they joined battle and routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng.
units.literal: The next day they joined battle and greatly defeated Tao at Jingcheng.

units.zh: 進檢校司空，實封六百戶。
units.en: He was promoted to Acting Minister of Works with a fief of six hundred households.
units.literal: He was advanced to Acting Minister of Works with an actual fief of six hundred households.

units.zh: 貞元初，朝京師，詔還所鎮。
units.en: Early in the Zhenyuan era he came to court and was ordered back to his command.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he came to court at the capital; an edict ordered him back to his command.

units.zh: 抱真喜士，聞世賢者，必欲與之遊，雖小善，皆卑禮厚幣數千里邀致之，至無可錄，徐徐以禮謝。
units.en: Baozhen delighted in scholars and sought out the worthy wherever he heard of them, sending humble invitations and rich gifts across thousands of li even for modest talents. When a guest proved unworthy, he dismissed him with courtesy.
units.literal: Baozhen delighted in scholars; hearing of worthy men of the age, he always wished to associate with them; even for small merits he used humble rites and rich gifts to invite them from thousands of li; when there was nothing worth recording, he slowly dismissed them with courtesy.

units.zh: 會天下稍無事，乃飾台沼以自娛。
units.en: As the realm grew quieter, he adorned terraces and ponds for his own pleasure.
units.literal: When the empire was somewhat without affairs, he then adorned terraces and ponds for his own pleasure.

units.zh: 好方士，謂不死可致。
units.en: He favored Daoist adepts and believed immortality could be attained.
units.literal: He favored alchemical masters and held that immortality could be attained.

units.zh: 有孫季長者為治丹，且曰：「服此當仙去。」
units.en: A man named Sun Jichang prepared elixirs for him, saying, "Take this and you will ascend as an immortal."
units.literal: There was one Sun Jichang who prepared elixir for him and said: "If you take this you ought to ascend as an immortal."

units.zh: 抱真表署幕府。
units.en: Baozhen had him appointed to his staff.
units.literal: Baozhen memorialized to appoint him to the staff.

units.zh: 嘗語左右曰：「秦、漢君不偶此，我乃得之，後升天，不復見公等矣。」
units.en: He told his attendants, "The emperors of Qin and Han never had this opportunity—I have found it. When I ascend to heaven I shall not see you again."
units.literal: He once told those at his side: "The rulers of Qin and Han did not chance upon this; I have obtained it; afterward I shall ascend to Heaven and will not see you gentlemen again."

units.zh: 夜夢駕鶴，寤而刻寓鶴，衣羽服，習乘之。
units.en: He dreamed one night of riding a crane; on waking he had a crane carved in relief, donned feather robes, and practiced mounting it.
units.literal: At night he dreamed of riding a crane; waking, he carved a crane in relief, wore feather robes, and practiced riding it.

units.zh: 後益惑厭勝，因疾，請降官，七讓司空，還為左僕射。
units.en: He grew ever more absorbed in sorcery and talismans. When illness struck he asked to be reduced in rank, declining the Ministry of Works seven times until he was left as Left Vice Director.
units.literal: Later he was increasingly deluded by sorcery and talismans; because of illness he requested reduction of rank; seven times he declined the Ministry of Works and returned to Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 餌丹二萬丸，不能食，且死，醫以彘肪穀漆下之。
units.en: He swallowed twenty thousand elixir pills, could no longer eat, and was near death. Physicians purged him with pig fat and lacquer.
units.literal: He ingested twenty thousand pills of elixir, could not eat, and was near death; physicians used pig fat and lacquer to purge him downward.

units.zh: 疾少間，季長曰：「危得仙，何自棄也？」
units.en: When he briefly improved, Jichang said, "You were on the verge of immortality—why throw that away?"
units.literal: When his illness eased slightly, Jichang said: "You were on the verge of becoming an immortal—why abandon it yourself?"

units.zh: 益服三千丸，卒，年六十二。
units.en: He took three thousand more pills and died at sixty-two.
units.literal: He took three thousand more pills and died, aged sixty-two.

units.zh: 抱真子 緘其子殿中侍御史緘匿喪，與其屬盧會昌元仲經謀，會諸將，仲經詭抱真令曰：「吾疾不任事，令緘典軍，勉佐之。」
units.en: Baozhen's son Jian, a Palace Attendant Censor, concealed his father's death. With his subordinates Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen's name: "My illness prevents me from governing. Jian shall command the army—assist him faithfully."
units.literal: Baozhen's son: Jian. His son, Palace Attendant Jian, concealed the death; with his subordinate Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he plotted; they assembled the generals; Zhongjing forged Baozhen's order, saying: "My illness prevents me from managing affairs; I order Jian to command the army—strive to assist him."

units.zh: 副使李說及諸校俯首，皆嘸曰；
units.en: Deputy Commissioner Li Shuo and the commanders bowed their heads and murmured assent;
units.literal: Deputy Commissioner Li Shuo and the various commanders bowed their heads; all murmured assent;

units.en: "Agreed."
units.literal: "Agreed."

units.zh: 緘盛服出，眾拜之，悉發府庫勞軍。
units.en: Jian appeared in full regalia; the officers bowed to him and the treasury was opened to reward the troops.
units.literal: Jian came out in full dress; the masses bowed to him; the entire treasury was opened to reward the army.

units.zh: 會昌即為抱真表，翌日，令諸將署章，請以節付緘。
units.en: Huichang immediately sent a memorial in Baozhen's name; the next day he had the generals sign a petition asking that command be given to Jian.
units.literal: Huichang immediately memorialized for Baozhen; the next day he had the generals sign a petition asking that the command be given to Jian.

units.zh: 天子已聞抱真喪，遣使者馳入軍，詔以事屬大將王延貴。
units.en: The emperor had already learned of Baozhen's death and sent an envoy racing to the army, ordering that command pass to the senior general Wang Yangui.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven had already heard of Baozhen's death and sent an envoy galloping into the army, ordering that affairs be entrusted to the great general Wang Yangui.

units.zh: 緘謾若抱真疾，請詰朝見，凡三日，緘乃出見使者，陳兵甚嚴。
units.en: Jian pretended Baozhen was merely ill and asked to receive the envoy the next morning. For three days he delayed; when he finally appeared before the envoy, his troops were drawn up in strict array.
units.literal: Jian pretended as if Baozhen were ill and requested to see [the envoy] the next morning; for three days in all; only then did Jian come out to see the envoy, arraying troops very strictly.

units.zh: 使者曰：「朝廷已知公薨，詔以兵屬延貴，君速歸發喪。」
units.en: The envoy said, "The court already knows your father is dead. Command passes to Yangui by edict. Return at once and begin the mourning."
units.literal: The envoy said: "The court already knows the lord has died; an edict places the troops under Yangui; sir, quickly return and begin the mourning."

units.zh: 緘愕然，謂諸將曰：「詔不許，若何？」
units.en: Jian was stunned. He asked the generals, "The edict forbids it—what now?"
units.literal: Jian was startled and said to the generals: "The edict does not permit it—what then?"

units.zh: 眾不對。
units.en: No one answered.
units.literal: The crowd did not answer.

units.zh: 乃遽以印鑰上監軍，始發喪。
units.en: He hastily surrendered the seal and keys to the army supervisor and only then began the mourning rites.
units.literal: He then hastily turned over the seal and keys to the army supervisor and only then began the mourning.

units.zh: 使者趣延貴視事，護緘赴東都，仲經逃諸外，捕殺之，會昌得不坐。
units.en: The envoy pressed Yangui to take command and escorted Jian to the Eastern Capital. Zhongjing fled and was hunted down and killed; Huichang escaped punishment.
units.literal: The envoy urged Yangui to take up affairs, escorted Jian to the Eastern Capital; Zhongjing fled abroad and was captured and killed; Huichang was not punished.

units.zh: 始，緘遣將陳榮以書抵武俊，假其財。
units.en: Earlier Jian had sent the general Chen Rong to Wang Wujun with a letter asking to borrow funds.
units.literal: Earlier, Jian had sent the general Chen Rong with a letter to Wujun to borrow his funds.

units.zh: 武俊怒曰；
units.en: Wujun said in anger,
units.literal: Wujun said in anger:

units.zh: 「吾與乃公善者，恭王命，非同惡也。
units.en: "I was your father's friend out of loyalty to the throne, not as a fellow rebel.
units.literal: "I was on good terms with your father out of respect for the royal command, not as fellow evildoers.

units.zh: 今聞已亡，誰詐其子使不俟朝制邪？」
units.en: Now I hear he is dead—who has deceived his son into defying the court's orders?"
units.literal: Now I hear he is already dead—who has deceived his son into not awaiting court regulations?"

units.zh: 囚榮而讓緘焉。
units.en: He imprisoned Chen Rong and rebuked Jian.
units.literal: He imprisoned Rong and reproached Jian for it.

units.zh: 詔贈抱真太保。
units.en: An edict posthumously made Baozhen Grand Guardian.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made Baozhen Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 路嗣恭，字懿範，京兆三原人，始名劍客，以世廕為鄴尉。
units.en: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, came from Sanyuan in Jingzhao. Originally named Jianke, he entered office through hereditary privilege as adjutant of Ye.
units.literal: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao; his original name was Jianke; through hereditary privilege he became Commandery Adjutant of Ye.

units.zh: 席豫黜陟河朔，表為蕭關令，連徙神烏、姑臧二縣，考績為天下最。
units.en: When Xi Yu reformed official appointments in Hebei, Sigong was recommended as magistrate of Xiaoguan, then served in succession at Shenwu and Guzang; his performance reviews ranked first in the empire.
units.literal: Xi Yu promoted and demoted officials in Hebei; [Sigong] was recommended as Magistrate of Xiaoguan, then transferred in succession to the two counties of Shenwu and Guzang; his examination record ranked highest in the empire.

units.zh: 玄宗以為可嗣漢魯恭，因賜名。
units.en: Xuanzong judged him a worthy successor to the virtuous Han magistrate Lu Gong and granted him the name Sigong.
units.literal: Xuanzong deemed him able to succeed Han's Lu Gong, and therefore granted him the name [Sigong].

units.zh: 轉渭南令，主杜化、東陽二驛。
units.en: He was transferred to magistrate of Weinan, overseeing the Duhua and Dongyang post stations.
units.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Weinan, in charge of the two post stations of Duhua and Dongyang.

units.zh: 時關畿用兵，使人系道，嗣恭儲具有素，而民不擾。
units.en: With war raging in the capital region and couriers choking the roads, Sigong had long laid up supplies, and the people were not disturbed.
units.literal: At that time the Guan region was at war; envoys filled the roads; Sigong had long stored supplies, and the people were not disturbed.

units.zh: 後為郭子儀朔方節度留後，大將孫守亮擁重兵，驕蹇不受制，嗣恭因稱疾，守亮至，即殺之，一軍皆震。
units.en: Later, as acting commissioner under Guo Ziyi's Shuofang command, he faced the arrogant general Sun Shouliang, who held a large force and refused obedience. Sigong feigned illness; when Shouliang came to call, he had him killed at once, and the whole army was shaken.
units.literal: Later he was Acting Military Commissioner of Guo Ziyi's Shuofang command; the great general Sun Shouliang held heavy troops, was arrogant and obstinate and would not accept control; Sigong therefore feigned illness; when Shouliang came, he was immediately killed, and the whole army was shaken.

units.zh: 永泰三年，檢校刑部尚書，知省事。
units.en: In the third year of Yongtai he was made Acting Minister of Justice with charge of court affairs.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongtai he was made Acting Minister of Justice and managed court affairs.

units.zh: 出為江西觀察使，以善治財賦稱。
units.en: He was sent out as observation commissioner of Jiangxi and won renown for skill in managing revenue.
units.literal: He went out as Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi and was famed for skill in managing finances and taxes.

units.zh: 有賈明觀者，素事魚朝恩，朝恩誅，當坐死，宰相元載納其賂，遣效力江西，將行，居民數萬懷瓦石候擊，載諭市吏禁止，乃得去。
units.en: Jia Mingguan had long served the eunuch Yu Chaoen. When Chaoen was executed Jia deserved death, but Chancellor Yuan Zai took his bribe and sent him to serve in Jiangxi. As he was about to leave, tens of thousands of townspeople gathered with stones to kill him; only when Zai ordered the market officers to restrain them could he depart.
units.literal: There was one Jia Mingguan who had long served Yu Chaoen; when Chaoen was executed he ought to have been put to death; Chancellor Yuan Zai accepted his bribe and sent him to serve in Jiangxi; as he was about to depart, tens of thousands of residents carried tiles and stones waiting to strike him; Zai ordered market officers to forbid it, and only then could he leave.

units.zh: 魏少游畏載，常回容之，及嗣恭代少遊，即日杖死。
units.en: Wei Shaoyou, fearing Zai, had long indulged Jia. When Sigong replaced Shaoyou, he had Jia beaten to death that same day.
units.literal: Wei Shaoyou feared Zai and constantly indulged him; when Sigong replaced Shaoyou, that same day he had him beaten to death.

units.zh: 大曆八年，嶺南將哥舒晃殺節度使呂崇賁，五嶺大擾。
units.en: In the eighth year of Dali the Lingnan general Geshu Huang killed Military Commissioner Lü Chongbin, throwing the Five Ridges into turmoil.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Dali the Lingnan general Geshu Huang killed Military Commissioner Lü Chongbin, and the Five Ridges were greatly disturbed.

units.zh: 詔嗣恭兼嶺南節度使，封冀國公。
units.en: Sigong was ordered to take concurrent command of Lingnan and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
units.literal: An edict made Sigong concurrently Military Commissioner of Lingnan and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ji.

units.zh: 嗣恭募勇敢士八千人，以流人孟瑤、敬冕為才，擢任之。
units.en: Sigong recruited eight thousand brave men and, recognizing talent in the exiles Meng Yao and Jing Mian, promoted them to command.
units.literal: Sigong recruited eight thousand brave men; he deemed the exiles Meng Yao and Jing Mian talented and promoted them to office.

units.zh: 使瑤督大軍當其沖，冕率輕兵由間道出不意，遂斬晃及支党萬餘，築屍為京觀。
units.en: Yao led the main force against the enemy front while Mian took light troops by a hidden route to strike from behind. They beheaded Huang and more than ten thousand of his followers and built a mound of their corpses.
units.literal: He had Yao command the great army to meet the enemy head-on; Mian led light troops by a hidden path to strike unexpectedly; they then beheaded Huang and more than ten thousand of his followers and built the corpses into a victory mound.

units.zh: 俚洞魁宿為惡者，皆族夷之。
units.en: The Li cave chiefs and elders who had done evil were exterminated to the last of their clans.
units.literal: The chieftains and elders of the Li caves who had done evil were all exterminated to the clan.

units.zh: 還為檢校兵部尚書，復知省事。
units.en: He returned as Acting Minister of War and again managed court affairs.
units.literal: He returned as Acting Minister of War and again managed court affairs.

units.zh: 嗣恭起州縣吏，以課治進至顯官，及晃事株戮舶商，沒其財數百萬私有之，代宗惡焉，故賞不酬功。
units.en: Sigong had risen from a county clerk through merit in governance to high office. In the Huang affair he executed merchant sailors wholesale and seized millions in private wealth. Daizong despised this, and Sigong's rewards never matched his achievements.
units.literal: Sigong rose from a county and district clerk, advanced through examination of governance to eminent office; in the Huang affair he executed merchant sailors root and branch, confiscated their wealth of several million and kept it privately; Daizong detested this, and therefore rewards did not match his merit.

units.zh: 德宗立，陰賕宰相楊炎，炎錄前效，更拜兵部尚書、東都留守。
units.en: When Dezong succeeded, Sigong secretly bribed Chancellor Yang Yan, who cited his past service and reappointed him Minister of War and resident of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: When Dezong took the throne, [Sigong] secretly bribed Chancellor Yang Yan; Yan recorded his past merit and again appointed him Minister of War and Resident of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 俄加懷鄭汝陝河陽三城節度、東都畿觀察使。
units.en: Soon after he was also made military commissioner of the Three Cities circuit and observation commissioner of the Eastern Capital metropolitan region.
units.literal: Shortly he was given the additional posts of Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Huai, Zheng, Ru, Shan, and Heyang, and Observation Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Metropolitan Circuit.

units.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈左僕射。
units.en: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made Left Vice Director.
units.literal: He died, aged seventy-one; posthumously made Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 子應、恕。
units.en: His sons were Ying and Shu.
units.literal: Sons: Ying and Shu.

units.zh: 子 應應，字從眾，以廕為著作郎。
units.en: His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by privilege as a Gentleman Compiler.
units.literal: Son: Ying. Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, through privilege entered office as Drafting Secretary.

units.zh: 貞元初，出為虔州刺史，詔嗣父封。
units.en: Early in the Zhenyuan era he was made prefect of Qianzhou and ordered to inherit his father's title.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he went out as Prefect of Qianzhou; an edict ordered him to inherit his father's enfeoffment.

units.zh: 鑿贛石梗嶮以通舟道。
units.en: He cut through the obstructing crags at Gan Rock to open the river route to navigation.
units.literal: He cut through the obstructing crags of Gan Rock to open the water route for boats.

units.zh: 德宗時，李泌為相，號得君。
units.en: Under Dezong, Li Bi served as chancellor and was known as a favorite of the emperor.
units.literal: In Dezong's time Li Bi was chancellor and was called one who had won the ruler.

units.zh: 帝嘗曰：「誰於卿有恩者，朕能報之。」
units.en: The emperor once said, "Tell me who has been kind to you, and I will repay them."
units.literal: The emperor once said: "Whoever has shown you kindness, I can repay them."

units.zh: 泌乃言：「曩為元載所疾，謫江西，路嗣恭與載厚，臣嘗畏之。
units.en: Bi replied, "Long ago Yuan Zai hated me and had me demoted to Jiangxi. Lu Sigong was close to Zai, and I feared him.
units.literal: Bi then said: "Formerly I was hated by Yuan Zai and was demoted to Jiangxi; Lu Sigong was close to Zai, and I once feared him.

units.zh: 會與其子應並驅，馬齧其脛，臣惶恐不自安，應閟不言，勉起見父。
units.en: Once I rode alongside his son Ying when a horse bit my shin. I was terrified, but Ying said nothing and forced himself up to see his father.
units.literal: It happened that I rode side by side with his son Ying; a horse bit my shin; I was fearful and ill at ease; Ying kept it secret and did not speak, then with effort rose to see his father.

units.zh: 臣常愧其長者，思有以報。」
units.en: I have long felt ashamed before his forbearance and wished to repay it."
units.literal: I have often been ashamed before his magnanimity and wished to repay it."

units.zh: 帝曰：「善。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Good."
units.literal: The emperor said: "Good."

units.zh: 即日加應檢校屯田郎中，服金紫。
units.en: That same day Ying was made Acting Director of the Bureau of State Farms and granted the gold-and-purple insignia of rank.
units.literal: That same day Ying was given the additional post of Acting Director of the Bureau of State Farms and wore gold and purple.

units.zh: 累遷宣歙池觀察使，封襄陽郡王。
units.en: He rose to observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi and was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Observation Commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi and enfeoffed as Prince of Xiangyang Commandery.

units.zh: 李錡反，應發鄉兵救湖、常二州，以故錡不能拔。
units.en: When Li Qi rebelled, Ying sent local militia to relieve Hu and Chang prefectures, preventing Qi from capturing them.
units.literal: When Li Qi rebelled, Ying sent local militia to rescue the two prefectures of Hu and Chang; because of this Qi could not take them.

units.zh: 元和六年，以疾授左散騎常侍，卒，諡曰靖。
units.en: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, ill health led to his appointment as Left Regular Cavalier; he died and was given the posthumous name Tranquil.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, because of illness he was made Left Regular Cavalier; he died; posthumous title Tranquil.

units.zh: 子 恕恕，字體仁。
units.en: His son Shu, courtesy name Tiren.
units.literal: Son: Shu. Shu, courtesy name Tiren.

units.zh: 從嗣恭討哥舒晃，授檢校工部員外郎，得從便宜，擢降將伊慎用之。
units.en: Serving under Sigong against Geshu Huang, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Works with discretionary authority and promoted the surrendered general Yi Shen to command.
units.literal: Following Sigong in the campaign against Geshu Huang, he was appointed Acting Vice Minister of Works with discretion to act as needed; he promoted the surrendered general Yi Shen and employed him.

units.zh: 賊平，恕功多。
units.en: When the rebellion was suppressed, Shu had earned great merit.
units.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Shu's merit was great.

units.zh: 嗣恭節度河陽也，恕為懷州刺史，年才三十，楊炎用捍魏博，為時嗤詆。
units.en: When Sigong held Heyang, Shu was made prefect of Huaizhou at only thirty. Yang Yan used him to block Weibo—a appointment widely mocked.
units.literal: When Sigong was military commissioner of Heyang, Shu was Prefect of Huaizhou, only thirty years old; Yang Yan used him to block Weibo; contemporaries mocked and reviled this.

units.zh: 累遷鄜坊、宣歙觀察使。
units.en: He later served as observation commissioner of Fu-Fang and of Xuan-She.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Observation Commissioner of Bin and Fang, and of Xuan and She.

units.zh: 坐事貶吉州刺史。
units.en: For an offense he was demoted to prefect of Jizhou.
units.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Prefect of Jizhou.

units.zh: 以右散騎常侍致仕，卒，贈洪州都督。
units.en: He retired as Right Regular Cavalier, died, and was posthumously made governor of Hongzhou.
units.literal: As Right Regular Cavalier he retired from office; he died; posthumously made Governor of Hongzhou.
